mainTopic: How the ברייתא extends the עריות of a wife's family to further generations, and why a man's own grandmother is not liable to שריפה through the same comparison.
overview: The amud explains a ברייתא about relatives in a wife's family who are forbidden as עריות. אביי reads the ברייתא as treating a man's own granddaughters like his wife's descendants. רבא, in the name of רב יצחק בר אבודימי, builds this with a two-link chain: הנה–הנה, then זמה–זמה. The גמרא next asks what 'below like above' means. It concludes that the wife's grandmothers are treated like the mother-in-law, and corrects the wording to 'above like below.' אביי explains that the word זמה extends the איסור to three generations above, like the three below. רב אשי instead keeps the original wording and reads 'below' as less strict. The גמרא then asks why a man's own grandmother should not be forbidden with שריפה. אביי answers from ״אִמְּךָ הִיא״, and רבא shows that the derivation fails under both methods of using a גזירה שוה. The refutation of the second method begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי explains what the ברייתא is really asking
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the ברייתא as asking how his own descendants are treated like his wife's descendants, learned through the word זמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what the ברייתא means. How do we know to treat a relative who comes from him like a relative who comes from her? 'זמה' is said here, and 'זמה' is said there, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי clears up a difficulty from before by explaining the real question the ברייתא is asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the ברייתא is about the man's own relatives (his granddaughters) and his wife's relatives (her daughter and granddaughters). The source it gives for treating them the same is a גזירה שוה on the word זמה. The 'etc.' means the ברייתא finishes the comparison in the usual way.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Used to explain or re-read a source.
A close relative
Coming from him / from her, meaning his relatives versus his wife's relatives
Lewdness. The word the תורה uses for certain family עריות
It says here... and it says there. The formula for a גזירה שוה

steps.confusionAlert: 'From him' does not mean the man himself. It means his own descendants, such as his son's daughter. 'From her' means his wife's descendants.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
From where do we know to treat a relative who comes from him
phrases.notes: 'From him' means his own descendants, like his son's daughter or his daughter's daughter.

phrases.english: like a relative who comes from her?
It says here "lewdness"
and it says there "lewdness," etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-reads the ברייתא from the previous section to solve an earlier difficulty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא asks how his descendants are treated like hers, and answers with זמה–זמה.

steps.title: But lewdness is not written by his own relatives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the word זמה is missing from the פסוק about his own granddaughters, so how can a זמה–זמה link apply to them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But by his own relatives, the word 'זמה' is not written!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's reading. A גזירה שוה on 'זמה' needs that word to appear in both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about his son's daughter and daughter's daughter (ויקרא 18:10) never uses the word זמה. So the comparison אביי offered seems to have nothing to grab onto on his side.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so... Opens a challenge
His own
It is not written

phrases.english: But regarding his own relative,
"lewdness" is not written in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בִּשְׁאֵר דִּידֵיהּ לָא כְּתִיבָא בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source אביי gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's זמה–זמה derivation for his own relatives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה שוה needs the shared word in both פסוקים, and זמה is missing from ויקרא 18:10.

steps.title: A two-step chain: הנה, then זמה
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רב יצחק בר אבודימי, links his relatives to hers through the word הנה, and then links hers onward through זמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב יצחק בר אבודימי told me: It is learned from 'הנה'–'הנה', and it is learned from 'זמה'–'זמה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the objection by building a chain of two גזירה שוה links instead of just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His granddaughters' פסוק (ויקרא 18:10) shares the word הנה with her relatives' פסוק (ויקרא 18:17). That פסוק also says זמה, which links it to ויקרא 20:14. Through this middle link, his relatives get the same law, even though זמה never appears by them directly.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes, meaning it is learned from
'They' or 'theirs.' The shared word in both פסוקים
A teaching that links two פסוקים through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: The equation of his relatives to hers works through a chain. First הנה–הנה (18:10 with 18:17), then זמה–זמה (18:17 with 20:14).

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לִי רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי,
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avudimi told me:
It is learned from "henna" and "henna",
it is learned from "lewdness" and "lewdness".

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲמַר לִי רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי, אָתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a middle link to the derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the זמה link could not reach his relatives.
steps.terutzMaskana: הנה connects his relatives to hers, and from there זמה carries the law forward.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the ברייתא: below like above
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא about treating 'below' like 'above,' in order to examine it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: How do we know to treat 'below' like 'above'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next discussion by quoting a new phrase from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. The phrase 'below like above' is unclear, and the next steps try to figure out which relatives it refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: Below like above, meaning one generation treated like another

phrases.english: The Master said:
From where do we know to treat below like above?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מִנַּיִן לַעֲשׂוֹת לְמַטָּה כִּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא teaches that relatives 'below' are treated like those 'above.'

steps.title: What does below like above mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which relatives the phrase is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'below like above'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the unclear phrase it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We need to know which generation is 'below' and which is 'above' before we can understand the ruling. The next steps test two possible answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is...

phrases.english: What is "below like above"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״לְמַטָּה כִּלְמַעְלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the quote in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which relatives are the 'below' and the 'above.'

steps.title: Not her granddaughters, since they appear together
steps.stepSummary: Reading it as her granddaughters being like her daughter is rejected, because all of them are in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means her son's daughter and her daughter's daughter are like her daughter, that cannot be, because they come together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one meaning and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her daughter and her granddaughters are all listed in ויקרא 18:17. Nothing needs to be 'learned' from one to the other, so the ברייתא cannot be asking about them.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. Introduces a suggestion
Together with each other
They come, meaning they appear in the text

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא בַּת בְּנָהּ וּבַת בִּתָּהּ כְּבִתָּהּ,
phrases.english: If you say her son's daughter and her daughter's daughter are like her daughter,
they come together!
phrases.notes: They're all in one פסוק, ויקרא 18:17, so there's nothing to learn from one to another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא בַּת בְּנָהּ וּבַת בִּתָּהּ כְּבִתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a first answer to step 5 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested meaning that her granddaughters are like her daughter
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: All of them appear in the same פסוק, so no derivation is needed.

steps.title: It means the grandmothers are like the mother-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the phrase refers to his father-in-law's mother and his mother-in-law's mother, who are treated like his mother-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his father-in-law's mother and his mother-in-law's mother are like his mother-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to what the phrase means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two grandmothers of his wife are not written in the תורה. So they truly need to be learned from his mother-in-law, who is written. That makes this a real derivation, unlike the rejected suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
His father-in-law
His mother-in-law

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אֵם חָמִיו וְאֵם חֲמוֹתוֹ כַּחֲמוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: Rather, his father-in-law's mother and his mother-in-law's mother are like his mother-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֵם חָמִיו וְאֵם חֲמוֹתוֹ כַּחֲמוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The grandmothers of his wife are treated like his mother-in-law.

steps.title: But that is above like below
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that grandmothers are a generation above the mother-in-law, so the phrase should say 'above like below.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this 'below like above'? It is 'above like below'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the new answer does not fit the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grandmothers are the higher generation, and they are being learned from the lower one (the mother-in-law). So the direction of the phrase is backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: This
Above like below

phrases.english: Is this "below like above"?
It is "above like below"!
phrases.notes: The grandmothers are the generation above, and they're the ones being learned from the mother-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי ״לְמַטָּה כִּלְמַעְלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 7 fits the ברייתא's words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fit between step 7's explanation and the phrase 'below like above'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case learns the higher generation from the lower one, which is the opposite of what the phrase says.

steps.title: Fix the wording to above like below
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the ברייתא to read 'above like below.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'above like below.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps its explanation and simply changes the ברייתא's wording to match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meaning from step 7 stands: his wife's grandmothers are like his mother-in-law. Only the phrase is flipped so that it describes the direction correctly.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא should read 'above like below.' The father-in-law's mother and the mother-in-law's mother are treated like the mother-in-law.

phrases.english: Teach: "above like below."

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנִי: ״לְמַעְלָה כִּלְמַטָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'below like above' seemed to contradict the explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'above like below.' The grandmothers are like the mother-in-law.

steps.title: How can the word זמה be written about relatives the Torah never mentions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's גזירה שוה. The grandmothers of the wife are not written in the תורה, so the word ״זִמָּה״ cannot be written about them either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the ברייתא says, ״'Lewdness' is stated here and 'lewdness' is stated there.″ But how can that be? These relatives are not even written in the תורה. Is the word 'lewdness' written about them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question on the ברייתא. A גזירה שוה needs the same word written in both places, but here one side, the grandmothers, is not written at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the ברייתא is about his father-in-law's mother and his mother-in-law's mother. These women are learned out by דרשה, not written in a פסוק. So the ברייתא's line about ״זִמָּה″ being stated ″here and there″ seems impossible, because the word is never written about them.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
Lewdness: the word the תורה uses for these forbidden relationships
It is stated here... and it is stated there: the standard wording of a גזירה שוה
Are not written in the תורה

phrases.english: If so,
'lewdness' is stated here
and 'lewdness' is stated there,
phrases.notes: This is the next line of the ברייתא. ויקרא 18:17 and ויקרא 20:14.

phrases.english: now, how can this be:
they themselves are not written,
so is 'lewdness' written about them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״זִמָּה״ וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״זִמָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the ברייתא's wording in step 9, the גמרא attacks the ברייתא's next line, the גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of a גזירה שוה on ״זִמָּה״ for the wife's grandmothers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה שוה needs the word written about the case itself. The grandmothers are not written in the תורה at all, so the word ״זִמָּה״ cannot be written about them.

steps.title: אביי: the word זמה extends the family line three generations up
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the גזירה שוה on ״זִמָּה″ is the very source that adds the grandmothers. Just as three generations below are forbidden, three generations above are forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: This is what the ברייתא means. From where do we know to treat three generations above like three generations below? 'Lewdness' is stated below and 'lewdness' is stated above. Just as below there are three generations, so too above there are three generations.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by reading the ברייתא differently. The גזירה שוה is not written about the grandmothers. It is the tool that brings them in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below, the פסוק itself forbids three generations: the wife, her daughter, and her granddaughter. Above, only the wife and her mother are written. The shared word ״זִמָּה״ teaches that the upper side also reaches three generations, so it includes her grandmothers. This answers step 10, because the word ״זִמָּה״ is written in the source פסוקים, not about the grandmothers.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: a rereading of a text
From where do we know?
Above: the wife's mother and grandmothers
Below: the wife's daughter and granddaughters
Three generations

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count the generations from the man himself. Both ″above″ and ″below″ are counted from his wife. Below means her daughter and granddaughter, and above means her mother and grandmother.

phrases.english: Abaye says:
this is what the baraita is saying:
From where do we know to make three generations above
like three generations below?
'Lewdness' is stated below
and 'lewdness' is stated above.
Just as below there are three generations,
so too above there are three generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by rereading what the גזירה שוה in the ברייתא is doing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to claim that ״זִמָּה״ is written directly about the grandmothers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה works between the written פסוקים above and below. It teaches that the upper side also includes three generations.

steps.title: אביי: the punishment and the warning each carry over to the other side
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the rest of the ברייתא. The punishment written above is applied below, and the warning written below is applied above.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as with the punishment the תורה made below like above, so too with the warning it made above like below.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his reading and explains the ברייתא's line ״above like below.″ He shows that the same link works in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment of burning is written only for the upper side, the wife's mother. Through ״זִמָּה״ it applies to the lower side too. The warning for three generations is written only for the lower side, so through the same link it applies to the upper side too. That is why the corrected wording from step 9, ″above like below,″ fits the warning.

keyTerms.meaning: Punishment: here, the death penalty
Warning: the actual prohibition in the תורה
Like above / like below

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the word ״זִמָּה״ connects both sides of the wife's family completely. The punishment moves from above to below, and the three-generation warning moves from below to above.

phrases.english: And just as with regard to punishment
the verse made below like above,
phrases.notes: Burning is written only for the wife's mother, and here it is applied to her daughter and granddaughter too.

phrases.english: so too with regard to the warning also
the verse made above like below.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה בָּעוֹנֶשׁ עָשָׂה לְמַטָּה כִּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's reading of the ברייתא and connects it to the corrected wording from step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was not clear why the corrected ברייתא says ″above like below.″
steps.terutzMaskana: For the warning, above is learned from below. For the punishment, below is learned from above.

steps.title: רב אשי: keep the original wording, because below means lower in strictness
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says there is no need to correct the ברייתא. ″Below″ refers to relatives who are lower in the strictness of the איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: Really, read it as it is taught. And what does ″below″ mean? Below in terms of the prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to the problem from step 8. He keeps the ברייתא's original wording, ″below like above,″ and explains the words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 assumed that ″above″ and ″below″ mean higher and lower generations. רב אשי says they describe how strict the איסור is. The grandmothers are further away and their איסור is less strict, so they are ″below.″ The ברייתא is making them like the closer mother-in-law, who is ″above.″

keyTerms.meaning: Really: introduces a defense of the original position or text
As it is taught, with no change to the wording
Prohibition, measured here by how strict it is

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to understand the ברייתא. The גמרא corrects it to ″above like below″ and reads the words as generations, which is the wording אביי then explains. רב אשי keeps ″below like above″ and reads the words as levels of strictness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a wording problem in a ברייתא can sometimes be solved by explaining a word differently instead of changing the text.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:
Actually, read it as it is taught,
and what is meant by 'below'?
Below in terms of the prohibition.
phrases.notes: The grandmothers are further away, so their איסור is less strict, and that makes them ″below″ the mother-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כִּדְקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of step 8 that replaces the correction made in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term instead of correcting the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ″Below″ meant a lower generation, so the ברייתא had to be corrected to ″above like below.″
steps.terutzMaskana: ″Below″ means lower in strictness of the איסור, so the original ″below like above″ is correct.

steps.title: Why not forbid his own grandmother too?
steps.stepSummary: If the גזירה שוה makes the wife's grandmother forbidden, maybe it should also make the man's own grandmother forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so: just as her mother's mother is forbidden, so too his mother's mother should be forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the ברייתא's derivation one step further. If the גזירה שוה adds the wife's grandmother, why not use the same comparison to add the man's own grandmother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used ״זִמָּה״ to add the wife's grandmothers. The challenge asks why the comparison should not also work between the wife's side and his own side, so that his mother's mother would be forbidden with the death penalty of שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her mother's mother, the wife's grandmother
His mother's mother, the man's own grandmother
So too he, meaning so too his relatives

phrases.aramaic: אִי: מָה הִיא – אֵם אִמָּהּ אֲסוּרָה,
phrases.english: If so: just as for her, her mother's mother is forbidden,
phrases.notes: "Her" means the wife. Her grandmother is forbidden to the husband, based on step 11.

phrases.english: so too for him, his mother's mother should be forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי: מָה הִיא – אֵם אִמָּהּ אֲסוּרָה, אַף הוּא – אֵם אִמּוֹ אֲסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the reasoning of אביי's גזירה שוה to a new case in order to challenge it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the גזירה שוה of ״זִמָּה״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison adds the wife's grandmother, nothing seems to stop it from adding the man's own grandmother, with the punishment of שריפה.

steps.title: אביי: 'She is your mother' limits the punishment
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the פסוק ״אִמְּךָ הִיא״ limits the death penalty to his mother and leaves out his grandmother.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The verse says 'she is your mother.' You make him liable because of his mother, but you do not make him liable because of his mother's mother.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge with a פסוק. The words ״אִמְּךָ הִיא״ show that the punishment applies only to his actual mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״הִיא״ (she) is read as a limiting word: she, his mother, and nobody else. So no גזירה שוה can add a death penalty for his grandmother, because the תורה itself excludes her.

keyTerms.meaning: She is your mother (ויקרא 18:7)
You make him liable to punishment

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a limiting word in a פסוק can block a גזירה שוה from reaching further cases.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The verse says: "She is your mother,"
because of his mother you make him liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם אֵם אִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: but you do not make him liable because of his mother's mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אָמַר קְרָא ״אִמְּךָ הִיא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that limits the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה שוה would make him liable to שריפה for his own grandmother.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אִמְּךָ הִיא″ limits the liability to his mother only, so his grandmother is excluded.

steps.title: רבא: Under either method, it is not derived
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently: whichever method of using a גזירה שוה you follow, the man's grandmother does not come out liable to שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both according to the one who says 'learn from it and from it,' and according to the one who says 'learn from it but set it in its own place,' this is not derived.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the same challenge. He says the result does not follow under either of the two known methods of using a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two views on how a גזירה שוה works. Under דון מינה ומינה, the new case takes every detail from the source, including its punishment. Under דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, you learn only the basic law, and the details follow the rules of the new case. רבא claims that neither method makes his grandmother liable to שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it and from it: the derived case takes all the details of the source
Learn from it but set it in its own place: the derived case keeps its own details
It does not come out, meaning it cannot be derived

steps.confusionAlert: These two phrases sound almost the same. The difference is only about the details: in the first, everything is copied from the source, and in the second, only the basic law is copied.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Both according to the one who says "learn from it and from it,"

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְאַתְרַהּ״ –
phrases.english: and according to the one who says "learn from it but set it in its own place" –
phrases.notes: He means: copy the basic law, but keep the details that belong to the new case.

phrases.english: it is not derived.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״דּוּן מִינַּהּ וּמִינַּהּ״, וּבֵין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְאַתְרַהּ″ – לָא אָתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the קשיא of step 14, alongside אביי's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Answer based on how a גזירה שוה works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה שוה would make his grandmother forbidden with שריפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under both methods of applying a גזירה שוה, this result does not follow.

steps.title: How the first method seems to work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts explaining רבא by showing how דון מינה ומינה would seem to forbid his grandmother with שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says 'learn from it and from it': just as her mother's mother is forbidden, so too his mother's mother is forbidden. And from it: just as she is punished by burning, so too he is punished by burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It spells out what the first method would seem to produce, so that it can then show why this is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under דון מינה ומינה, the comparison passes along two things: first the איסור itself, and then its punishment, שריפה. This step only describes what the method seems to produce. רבא's point that it still does not work comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning, one of the four death penalties of בית דין
Also

phrases.english: According to the one who says: learn from it and from it,
just as for her, her mother's mother is forbidden –

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא נָמֵי אֵם אִמּוֹ אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: so too for him, his mother's mother is also forbidden.
And from it: just as she is with burning –
so too he is also with burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: דּוּן מִינַּהּ וּמִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining רבא's statement by working through the first method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under דון מינה ומינה, the comparison would seem to forbid his grandmother and also make him liable to שריפה. This sets up רבא's explanation of why the result still does not follow.

steps.title: First refutation: her mother is burned, but his mother is only stoned
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that שריפה is stricter than סקילה, the comparison breaks down. The wife's side is stricter, because her mother is punished with שריפה. His side is less strict, because his own mother is only punished with סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says burning is the more severe death, the comparison can be refuted. Her relatives are special, because her mother is punished by burning. Can you then say the same for his relatives, when his own mother is punished only by stoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins pushing back on the derivation from step 17. It shows that his relatives cannot learn from her relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only learn one case from another if the source case is not stricter. If שריפה is the harsher death, the wife's side is stricter, since her mother gets שריפה. His side is milder, since his mother gets סקילה. So the strict rule of her side cannot be copied over to his side.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning is the more severe death penalty (one opinion)
There is room to refute (to find a difference that breaks the comparison)
Death by stoning
"What about X... will you say about Y?" The standard way to point out a difference that breaks a comparison

steps.confusionAlert: ״היא״ (her) means the wife's relatives, and ״הוא״ (him) means the man's own relatives. These are the two sides being compared, so it is easy to mix them up.

phrases.english: According to the one who says: burning is more severe,
there is room to refute it.
What about "her" relatives?
phrases.notes: "Her" means the wife. The גמרא is pointing to what makes her side special.

phrases.english: They are special because her mother is punished by burning.
Will you say the same about "his" relatives,
where his own mother is punished only by stoning?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: שְׂרֵיפָה חֲמוּרָה, אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the derivation laid out in step 17, as part of explaining רבא in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The derivation from the wife's relatives to his own relatives, according to the view that שריפה is stricter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source case (the wife's side) is stricter than the target case (his side), so it cannot be used to teach a strict rule for his side.

steps.title: Second refutation: his grandmother cannot be stricter than his mother
steps.stepSummary: Still according to the view that שריפה is stricter: it makes no sense that his mother gets the milder סקילה while his grandmother, who is a more distant relative, gets the harsher שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: his mother is punished by stoning. Could his mother's mother be punished by burning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason why his grandmother cannot be liable to שריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A closer relative should not get a lighter punishment than a more distant one. His mother is closer to him than his grandmother is. If the mother gets only סקילה, giving the grandmother the harsher שריפה would turn the order upside down.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (introduces another argument)
His mother's mother (his grandmother)

phrases.english: And furthermore: his mother is punished by stoning,
so could his mother's mother be punished by burning?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: אִמּוֹ בִּסְקִילָה, אֵם אִמּוֹ בִּשְׂרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second refutation that also depends on שריפה being stricter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the more distant relative (grandmother) punished more harshly than the closer relative (mother).

steps.title: Third refutation: mother and grandmother should be treated the same
steps.stepSummary: On the wife's side, her mother and her grandmother get the same punishment. So on his side too, his mother and his grandmother should get the same punishment. His mother gets סקילה, not שריפה, so his grandmother would not get שריפה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: with her relatives, you did not make a difference between her mother and her mother's mother. So too with his relatives, you should not make a difference between his mother and his mother's mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third refutation. It uses the comparison itself to show that his grandmother should follow his mother's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you compare the two sides, you have to copy the pattern too. On her side, mother and grandmother are treated the same. On his side, that means the grandmother follows the mother, who gets סקילה. This argument does not depend on which death is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: You did not make a distinction
You should not make a distinction

phrases.english: And furthermore: just as with "her" relatives,
you did not make a distinction
between her mother and her mother's mother,
phrases.notes: Both are punished with burning, so they are treated the same.

phrases.english: so too with "his" relatives, also
you should not make a distinction
between his mother and his mother's mother?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: מָה הִיא לֹא חִלַּקְתָּ בָּהּ בֵּין אִמָּהּ לְאֵם אִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third refutation, which works without assuming שריפה is stricter.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Applying שריפה to his grandmother through the comparison.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison itself teaches that grandmother follows mother, and his mother gets סקילה, not שריפה.

steps.title: Even if stoning is more severe, the third refutation still blocks it
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that סקילה is stricter, the first two refutations do not work. But the third refutation still stands, so his grandmother does not get שריפה under this view either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says stoning is more severe, we still cannot derive it, because of this last difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its explanation of רבא. Under both opinions about which death is stricter, his grandmother is not liable to שריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two refutations depend on שריפה being harsher, so they fall away if סקילה is harsher. The third refutation (mother and grandmother are treated the same) does not depend on which death is stricter. So it blocks the derivation under this view too.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning is the more severe death penalty (the other opinion)
A difficulty or objection
We would derive it (here: we do not derive it)

steps.whatToRemember: Whichever death penalty is considered stricter, the גזירה שוה cannot make a man's own grandmother liable to שריפה. That is what רבא claimed in step 16.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says stoning is more severe,
because of this difficulty, we do not derive it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר סְקִילָה חֲמוּרָה, מֵהַאי קוּשְׁיָא לָא נְידוּנַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation by showing that the third refutation works even under the opposite opinion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under both views about which death is stricter, a man's own grandmother is not liable to שריפה through this comparison.

steps.title: Learning the grandmother prohibition with the softer method
steps.stepSummary: Under דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, his mother's mother is forbidden just like his wife's mother's mother. But the punishment stays fitted to his side, so it is סקילה, as with his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says we learn from the source but keep the law fitted to its own place: just as on her side her mother's mother is forbidden, so too on his side his mother's mother is forbidden. And keep it fitted to its place: there, on her side, the punishment is שריפה, but here, on his side, it is סקילה, as we found with his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It spells out what the second method, דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, would seem to produce, so that it can then show why even this fails, as רבא claimed in step 16. This method copies only the prohibition from the wife's side, not her side's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With דון מינה ומינה, everything gets copied, including the שריפה, and that led to problems. Here, with דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, we would copy only the basic rule, that the grandmother is forbidden. The punishment would come from his own side, so it would be סקילה as with his mother. The next step shows that even this derivation can be refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, but keep it in its own place: copy the basic rule, but keep the details that fit the new case
Her mother's mother: the wife's grandmother
His mother's mother: the man's own grandmother
As we found: pointing to a known case as the model

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two methods. דון מינה ומינה copies the punishment too, which gave שריפה. דון מינה ואוקי באתרה copies only the prohibition, so the punishment here becomes סקילה.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר, דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְאַתְרַהּ:
phrases.english: And according to the one who says: learn from it, but set it in its own place:
Just as with her, her mother's mother is forbidden,
phrases.notes: "Her" is the wife. Her grandmother is forbidden to the husband.

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא נָמֵי – אֵם אִמּוֹ אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: so too with him, his mother's mother is forbidden.
And set it in its own place:
it is there that the punishment is burning,
phrases.notes: "There" means the wife's family, and "here" in the next line means his own family.

phrases.english: but here it is stoning,
as we found with his mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר, דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְאַתְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having shown that the first method does not work, the גמרא now works through the second method named by רבא in step 16, setting it up so it can be refuted next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This step spells out what דון מינה ואוקי באתרה would seem to produce: his mother's mother forbidden, with סקילה like his mother. The גמרא does not accept this. רבא already said it is not derived (step 16), and step 23 begins the refutation.

steps.title: Setting up a refutation for the view that burning is stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that, according to the view that שריפה is stricter, this learning can be knocked down.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says שריפה is stricter, there is a way to refute this.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to show why even this softer learning does not work, at least for the view that שריפה is the stricter death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The refutation itself is spelled out at the start of the next amud. The point announced here is that the strength of the wife's side, where the punishment is שריפה, may make it a poor source for his side. The challenge is limited to the view that שריפה is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute: the learning can be knocked down
Burning is stricter: the view that שריפה is a harsher death than סקילה

phrases.english: According to the one who says burning is more severe,
there is a way to refute it:
phrases.notes: The actual refutation comes right after this, at the start of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׂרֵיפָה חֲמוּרָה, אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the attack on the learning from step 22, limited to the view that שריפה is stricter.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only according to the view that שריפה is stricter than סקילה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Announced here. The details are spelled out at the start of the next amud.
